summary.good.say: We found <count> <controls> working as intended, and the score counts them, so a change that breaks one lowers it.

summary.good-none.say: We found no controls working as intended, so the score gives credit for none.

say.one: <names> has the least risk, counting each finding by its severity.
say.many: <names> have the least risk, counting each finding by its severity.

say.one: <names> carries the most risk, counting each finding by its severity.
say.many: <names> carry the most risk, counting each finding by its severity.

summary.most-none.say: No area stands out when each finding counts by its severity.

summary.alone-including.say: <name> alone has <count> of the <total> findings, including <severe>.

say.one: <count> finding is critical, meaning a control is missing altogether, so start there.
say.many: <count> findings are critical, meaning a control is missing altogether, so start there.

say.one: <count> is high, where a control is in place and fails.
say.many: <count> are high, where a control is in place and fails.

say.one: The other <count> is medium, low or info.
say.many: The other <count> are medium, low or info.

say.one: Fixing the <severe> <findings> removes the serious risk, and the other <count> is lower-priority hardening.
say.many: Fixing the <severe> <findings> removes the serious risk, and the other <count> are lower-priority hardening.

summary.serious-fix-only.say: Fixing the <severe> <findings> removes the serious risk.

say.one: No critical or high findings are open, and the <count> open finding is lower-priority hardening.
say.many: No critical or high findings are open, and the <count> open findings are lower-priority hardening.

summary.each-names-fix.say: Each finding names the change that fixes it.

summary.between.say: <names> hold <count> of the <total> findings between them.

summary.untouched.say: We read the code without running it and changed nothing in <whole>. Every finding cites the file and lines it rests on.

say.one: The <severe> finding is the one that changes the risk.
say.many: The <severe> findings are the ones that change the risk.

say.one: The review found <count> critical finding, and it comes first.
say.many: The review found <count> critical findings, and they come first.

summary.verdict-none.say: The review found no critical findings.

say.one: We found <count> control working, worth keeping as it is.
say.many: We found <count> controls working, worth keeping as they are.

summary.c-heaviest-holds.say: <name> holds <count> of the <total> findings, so with time for one area, start here.

summary.c-heaviest-holds-including.say: <name> holds <count> of the <total> findings, including <severe>, so with time for one area, start here.

summary.c-next-none.say: No other area comes close when each finding counts by its severity.

summary.c-mix.say: The mix is <critical> critical, <high> high, <medium> medium, <low> low and <info> info.

summary.c-critical-means.say: A critical finding means a control is missing, so it changes what the system can promise.

summary.c-weakness.say: Each finding is a weakness in a control that is already there.

say.one: The <severe> finding changes the risk, and fixing the other <depth> makes the system harder to break.
say.many: The <severe> findings change the risk, and fixing the other <depth> makes the system harder to break.

say.one: We found <count> control working, a place where we looked for a weakness and found the control doing its job.
say.many: We found <count> controls working, places where we looked for a weakness and found the control doing its job.

summary.c-good-none.say: We found no controls working as intended.

summary.c-clean-among.say: <count> disciplines found nothing to fix, among them <names>.

summary.c-one-found.say: The one discipline read found something to fix.

summary.c-all-found.say: All <count> disciplines found at least one thing to fix.

summary.c-unreached.say: A control the review didn't reach may still exist.

summary.c-confirmed.say: A second check confirmed or a scanner found <count> of the <total> findings, and the other <rest> rest on one reading, marked asserted.

summary.c-unconfirmed.say: Every finding rests on one reading, marked asserted, so check each against the code before acting on it.

summary.c-tiers.say: The work splits into <p0> to do first, <p1> near-term, <p2> should-fix and <p3> cleanup.

summary.c-share-spread.say: The heaviest area, <name>, has <share>% of the findings, so the work spreads across the system.
